records.name: Baker Point Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sequoia National Forest, Hot Springs Ranger District

extra.description: Baker Point Lookout is located in the Hot Springs District of the Sequoia National Forest in Township 24 S., Range 32 E., Section 10, and overlooks the Upper Kern River Canyon to the east as well as the west face of the Kern Plateau and to the west multiple drainages of the Bull Run Basin and Northeast slopes of the Greenhorn Range. Sitting at 7,754 feet, the Baker Point Lookout hovers on a granite peak 5,000 feet above the Kern River north of Kernville.

records.name: Bald Mtn Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sequoia National Forest, Cannell Ranger District

extra.description: Bald Mountain Lookout was built and became active in 1951. The lookout used today was constructed in 1955 from materials brought in via a mule train along trails before any roads existed to the area. Located in the Sequoia National Forest, Cannell Ranger District, Township 22 S, Range 34 E, Section 12, it is also used for BLM and Inyo Forest Fire Traffic. Bald Mountain Lookout is located at an elevation of 9,430 feet and is located off the Sherman Pass Road near Black Rock Station in the Southeastern most portion of the Sequoia National Forest.

records.name: Mt. Tom Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sierra National Forest, Minerets Ranger District

extra.description: Mt. Tom Lookout is located at an elevation of 9,018 feet, and is closed during the winter months due to heavy snow levels. There is access to the tower and surrounding area to the general public during the summer when the tower is open for service. The towers map location is Township 6 South, Range 26 East, Section 30 on the Sierra National Forest Map and is located in the State of California (County of Fresno), in the Sierra National Forest. The tower has a three story stair master built into the tower to reach the cab and stands 34 feet from the ground. :-))

extra.description: Breckenridge Lookout is located in the Sequoia National Forest, Greenhorn District, in Township 28 S, Range 32 E, Section 31, at an elevation of 7,548 feet, and is the Southern most lookout on the Sequoia National Forest. Breckenridge lookouts also man a patrol in the early morning hours and have continually been of great help to the BLM and Kern County Fire Fighters.

extra.description: Mule Peak Lookout was built in 1935 and is wood frame construction. Mule Peak is located in Township 22 S, Range 31 E, Section 15. Mule Peak is Located in Tulare County, California, at an elevation of 8,142 feet.

records.name: Musick Mtn Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sierra National Forest, Minerets Ranger District

extra.description: Musick Mountain Fire Lookout is located at an elevation of 6,775 feet, on U.S. Forest Service Map T9S, R24E, S1. The lookout was originally constructed in 1912 and was a compass type lookout. It was replaced in 1924 with a cab/cabin type of tower and was non-continuous staffing. In 1939 it was replaced with the current type of tower, 20 foot, H-Beam Steel Tower with a C-3(L)Cab. The tower has not been maintained and has been deteriorating over the years. It is now used as a communications tower.

extra.description: Deadwood Lookout Tower is located at T7S, R21E, S21 of the U.S.F.S. Map, at an elevation of 4,540 feet. The photo of the tower was taken during winter closure of the tower in 1993. The tower has been retired from active service since the end of the 1994 fire season and was staffed by paid or volunteer lookouts while it was in service. records.name: Delilah Pk Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sequoia National Forest, Hume Ranger District

extra.description: Delilah Lookout is located in the Hume District of the Sequoia National Forest in Township 13 S., Range 26 E., Section 11 at an elevation of 5,170 feet, and is approximately 45 miles East of Fresno, California, in the Southern Sierra. Delilah is not in operation continuously at this time, but is placed into use when fire danger is very high or volunteer lookouts are available. The original lookout was built pre 1916 with the tower built in 1924 with a cabin below and replaced in 1959 and in 1967 with a steel tower from Lemore Naval Air Force Base.

records.name: Redtop Fire Lookout
records.agency: CAL FIRE (CDF) -- Madera, Mariposa, Merced Ranger Unit

extra.description: Red Top Fire Lookout was constructed in or about 1938 on one acre of land. It is located at an elevation of 1,840 feet and is on Madera County Parcel located in the Southwest 1/4 of Section 22, Township 9 South, Range 20 East, Coarsegold, California. The lookout is West of State Highway 41 and North of County Road 406. It is located on private property and there is no public access to the site any longer.

records.name: Fence Meadow Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sierra National Forest, Kings River Ranger District

extra.description: Fence Meadow is a lookout located at map reference: T11S, R26E, S19, and sits on a high point located above the Kings River Canyon on the South end of Sierra National Forest.  Fence Meadow Lookout is one of two remaining lookouts on the Kings River Ranger District and remains in active service to this date. Constructed in 1934, the 14 x 14 foot, L-4 cab with a catwalk around it, and is mounted atop a 20 foot H-braced steel tower. One of only 18 L-4 cabs remaining in California, it has the newer style 1/4 inch solid pane windows. Fence Meadow Lookout is currently staffed with paid and volunteer fire lookouts.

records.name: Goat Mtn Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sierra National Forest, Bass Lake Ranger District

extra.description: There is not a lot of information available about Goat Mountain Lookout and is said to be a pre 1915 lookout. The lookout is located at an elevation of 4,634 feet and is found at map reference T7S, R22E, S34. The 1915 cabin building blew down in winter 1915-16. There is no record of use until 1934 when it was reconstructed. In fall 1935, winds shifted tower on the base, and it had to be reconstructed again, though it appears to be the same cab was used and the base was replaced with a Pacific Coast Steel tower. The tower is a 20 foot, H-B Steel L-4 Hip-2 built by Pacific Coast Steel Tower. The tower is no longer used for fire detection and is maintained as a radio relay site for the Forest Service now.

records.name: Tobias Pk Fire Lookout
records.agency: Sequoia National Forest, Hot Springs Ranger District

extra.description: Tobias Peak Lookout was built in 1935 and manned in 1936. Tobias has been, since it's inception a United States Forest Service, Sequoia National Forest, Hot Springs Ranger District Lookout and is located at an elevation of 9,292 feet. Located in Township 24S, Range 32E, Section 7, and is of wood frame construction and sits on a rock base. Tobias looks over the SanJuaquin Valley and has visability to Mt.Whitney as well as the Kaweahs (Great Western Divide), the west face of the Kern Plateau and the Golden Trout Wilderness as well as a view of the Paiutes and the Scoddie Mountains and a small part of the Kern River Valley.
